transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, I came in because... well, I'm having trouble with my eating. Once I start eating, it feels like I just disappear. It's like something else takes over completely, and even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I just keep going. I keep at it until I physically can't stand it anymore.
After these episodes happen, do you do anything to try to get rid of the food or prevent weight gain?

Yeah, I do. Um... after I eat like that, I usually end up going to a bathroom in my dorm, or sometimes I'll find a quiet floor in the library, and... I make myself throw up. I just get terrified that all that food is just sitting in my stomach, turning into weight. So I have to get rid of it.
To help me understand your physical health, could you tell me your current height and weight?

Um... I'm honestly not sure right now. I haven't really weighed myself lately. I kind of stopped looking at the scale because... well, it just messes with my head too much, so I don't know the exact number. And I'm not totally sure about my exact height either, to be honest. I just haven't kept track of it.
On average, how often do these episodes of eating and making yourself throw up happen each week?

Um, for most of this semester, it's been happening several times a week. It's definitely not just a once-in-a-while thing anymore. If I look back over at least the last few months... yeah, there really hasn't been a single week where the cycle stopped.
Even without knowing the exact numbers, have doctors or people in your life expressed concern that you are dangerously thin or significantly underweight?

No, not really. I mean, nobody's ever told me I look dangerously thin or anything like that. I'm pretty sure I just look like an average guy. No one's really made any comments about me being underweight.
